narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To illustrate the increase in contraceptive use in sub-Saharan Africa from 1990 to 2000, contrasting it with slower educational improvements.

units.meaning: In 1990, contraceptive use in the region was 16%.

basis.note: Table cell for contraceptive use in 1990.

accepted_routes: Contraceptive use stood at 16% at the start of the period.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A visible data mark or label for contraceptive use in 1990 must show 16%.
units.temporal_anchor: The narration clause establishing the 1990 starting point.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly show the 1990 starting value of 16%?

basis.note: Table cell for contraceptive use in 2000.

accepted_routes: Contraceptive use ended the 1990-2000 period at 22%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A visible data mark or label for contraceptive use in 2000 must show 22%.
units.temporal_anchor: The narration clause establishing the 2000 endpoint.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly show the 2000 endpoint value of 22%?

units.meaning: Between 1990 and 2000, contraceptive use rose by 6 percentage points, from 16% to 22%.

basis.note: Used with the 1990 value to derive the absolute change.

accepted_routes: Between 1990 and 2000, contraceptive use rose by 6 percentage points.
The gain from 1990 to 2000 was 6 points (16% to 22%).
Contraceptive use increased from 16% to 22%, a 6-percentage-point rise.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both the 1990 value and the 2000 value must be visible, or the 6-percentage-point difference must be explicitly labelled.
units.temporal_anchor: The narration clause describing the 1990-to-2000 increase.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state the absolute increase as 6 percentage points?

units.meaning: The 1990-to-2000 increase was about 37.5% relative to the 1990 level.
accepted_routes: The 1990-2000 increase was about 37.5% relative to the 1990 level.
Contraceptive use was roughly 38% higher in 2000 than in 1990.
The relative gain from 1990 to 2000 was a little over one third.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 1990 and 2000 values must be visible enough to support the relative comparison; if only one is shown, the 37.5% claim is unsupported.
units.temporal_anchor: An optional narration clause adding the relative-size comparison for 1990-2000.
units.reviewer_question: Is the derived relative increase of about 37.5% required, or is it optional context?

units.meaning: The 1990-2000 rise is part of an upward trend across all available years: 16%, 19%, 22%, 23.5%, 27.5%, and 30% from 1990 to 2014.

basis.note: First value in the available series.
Final value in the available series.

accepted_routes: Every measured year from 1990 to 2014 is higher than the previous one: 16%, 19%, 22%, 23.5%, 27.5%, 30%.
Contraceptive use follows an upward trend across all available years, not just 1990-2000.
The series rises from 16% in 1990 to 30% in 2014 without any measured decline.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The full sequence of values must be visible or labelled if the video claims a no-decline trend beyond 2000.
units.temporal_anchor: An optional post-2000 or full-series narration clause.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video include the longer 1990-2014 upward trend, or stay strictly within 1990-2000?

optional_valid: The 1995 midpoint value of 19% may be shown as an intermediate step within the 1990-2000 rise.
The later values 2005=23.5%, 2010=27.5%, and 2014=30% may be shown as extra post-2000 context.
The 1990-2014 increase of 14 percentage points (30 - 16 = 14) may be shown as optional context.
unsupported_to_avoid: Any claim about education improving slower or faster, or by any amount, because the table contains no education data.
Saying contraceptive use doubled from 1990 to 2000; 22% is 1.375 times 16%, not double.
Saying it exactly doubled from 1990 to 2014; 30% is 1.875 times 16%, not exactly double.
Causal explanations for why contraceptive use rose.
Values or regions not present in the table.
notes: The table contains only contraceptive-use percentages, so no education-contrast unit is proposed. The core 1990-2000 endpoint and 6-percentage-point change are required; the relative increase and longer trend are optional context.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
